_doc: GROWTH-1/2: the product manager's job is growth, not only bug fixes (owner directive 2026-11-12). This file is what the product manager loop reads: the share of shipped work that must be growth, the growth metrics with a baseline, a target and a horizon (the expected value today is the straight line between them), how work is classified, and the idea bank each metric draws its next experiment from. foundation/growth.py measures the mix and the metrics, foundation/pm.py runs the loop (targets, experiments, knobs, filing) and the executor prefers a growth item whenever the recent mix falls below the target. A growth item adds a capability, a surface, a reader or a customer path; a fix repairs something that was meant to work; maintenance keeps it running.
label: growth

products.what: ultrastable.io: the public front door, pilot path and agent-readable surfaces

metrics.what: human page views in the last 7 days (first-party, cookieless, bots excluded)
metrics.trigger: behind its trajectory opens the next growth item from the idea bank

metrics.what: distinct visitors in the last 7 days
metrics.trigger: behind its trajectory opens the next growth item from the idea bank

metrics.what: requests from bots and agents in the last 7 days (discovery documents, MCP, llms.txt)
metrics.trigger: behind its trajectory opens the next growth item from the idea bank

metrics.what: views of the pilot application page in the last 7 days
metrics.trigger: behind its trajectory opens the next growth item from the idea bank

pageviews_7d.title: GROW-7: one page per kind of system the product runs (club site, service fleet, research desk) with a deep link into the interview
pageviews_7d.desc: Add /use-cases and one page per system type from the VISION list, each with the loop, the measure, the upkeep and a typical monthly cost, linking into the interview. Paths: site/usecases.js, site/worker.js, site/site.test.mjs.

pageviews_7d.title: GROW-8: structured data (FAQPage, SoftwareApplication) on the core pages
pageviews_7d.desc: Add JSON-LD for FAQPage on /faq and SoftwareApplication on /product, generated from the same data as the visible text. Paths: site/worker.js, site/site.test.mjs.

visitors_7d.title: GROW-9: a share card per page generated from the live record
visitors_7d.desc: Generate Open Graph cards for /live, /demo and the case study showing the current scoreboard, so a shared link shows the system working. Paths: site/cards.js, site/worker.js.

visitors_7d.title: GROW-10: a weekly digest of what the system shipped, built from the changelog
visitors_7d.desc: A digest page and feed of the week's merged changes and clock health, ready for the existing double opt-in subscribe flow. Paths: site/digest.js, site/worker.js.

agent_hits_7d.title: GROW-11: markdown content negotiation for every page
agent_hits_7d.desc: Return a Markdown rendering of each page when the request sends Accept: text/markdown, with an x-markdown-tokens header, so agents read the site cheaply. Paths: site/worker.js, site/site.test.mjs.

agent_hits_7d.title: GROW-12: runnable examples for the MCP endpoint and the OpenAPI document
agent_hits_7d.desc: A /docs/agents page with copyable curl and client examples for every MCP tool, generated from the tool list. Paths: site/agentdocs.js, site/worker.js.

pilot_page_views_7d.title: GROW-13: a pilot FAQ answering price, data, hosting and exit
pilot_page_views_7d.desc: Answer the questions a pilot applicant has before applying (what it costs, where the data lives, who hosts it, how to leave), from the pilot offer data. Paths: site/pilotfaq.js, site/worker.js.

pilot_page_views_7d.title: GROW-14: a one-tap apply entry from the live record and the demo
pilot_page_views_7d.desc: Add an apply link with a short why to the live page and the demo, tagged so its conversion is measured. Paths: site/live.js, site/demo.js.

owner_note: Targets are first hypotheses chosen by the system: the baseline measured on 2026-11-12 (1310 page views, 564 visitors, 817 agent hits, 326 pilot page views in 7 days) plus 15 to 25 percent over 28 days. The product manager revises them from measured baselines, each change as a reviewed PR.
